summary: Provides simple fixes to the IANA IP Flow Information Export Entities registry, such as improving descriptions of some Information Elements, making citations of other registries consistent, and fixing broken pointers and orphaned section references.

plainLanguage.summary: A big reference list had typos and broken page numbers. This is a cleanup pass.

questions: how are ipfix information elements registered
subtitle: Cleanup and consistency improvements to the IP Flow Information Export registry.

tldr.problem: The IANA registry of IPFIX Information Elements had accumulated inconsistencies: vague descriptions, broken links, outdated registry references, and missing pointers to related IANA registries.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9710 systematically fixes these problems by rewriting descriptions for clarity, consolidating how references to other IANA registries are formatted, and correcting broken links and obsolete section references.
tldr.outcome: The IPFIX registry is now more maintainable and easier to extract values from programmatically, enabling collectors to automatically stay current with new IPFIX information elements.

facts.label: Categories of fixes
facts.value: 4 (description updates, registry pointers, consistent citations, miscellaneous)

today: RFC 9710 is a Proposed Standard from February 2025 that updates the IANA IP Flow Information Export Entities registry. It does not modify the IPFIX protocol itself (RFC 7011) or the information model (RFC 5102 and RFC 7012), only the clarity and consistency of the registry that catalogs Information Elements.

sections.title: Why This Cleanup Was Necessary
sections.content:
IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX), defined in RFC 7011, is a protocol for exporting network flow data. IPFIX uses Information Elements to describe the fields that can appear in flow records. The IANA registry of IPFIX Information Elements grew over time as different RFCs added new elements.

During work on RFC 9565 and RFC 9487, maintainers discovered that the registry needed cleanup. Some descriptions were unclear. Many entries referenced other IANA registries but did so inconsistently—some embedded the registry values in the description, others used bare URLs. References to registries were sometimes broken or pointed to outdated URLs. Some entries had orphaned section references or wrong abstract data types. RFC 9710 addresses these systematic issues by providing fixes that enable IANA to update the registry and make it programmatically extractable.
sections.plainLanguage: As the IPFIX registry grew, people added entries in different styles. Some descriptions were vague, some links were broken, and the way entries pointed to other lists was inconsistent. This RFC fixes all that.

sections.title: What Was Fixed
sections.content: The RFC organizes fixes into four categories. First, descriptions are improved for vague or incomplete Information Elements like sourceTransportPort and destinationTransportPort, adding support for DCCP alongside UDP, TCP, and SCTP. Second, entries that should reference existing IANA registries now have "Additional Information" pointers to those registries instead of embedding values inline. Third, descriptions for entries already pointing to registries are rewritten to use consistent formatting and correct registry names (for example, renaming informationElementDataType to IPFIX Information Element Data Types). Fourth, miscellaneous fixes correct broken links, orphaned section references, and clarify descriptions.
sections.plainLanguage: The fixes fall into types: make descriptions clearer, add pointers to related lists, standardize how links are written, and fix broken references.

sections.title: Improved Descriptions
sections.content:
Several Information Elements describing transport ports—sourceTransportPort, destinationTransportPort, collectorTransportPort, and exporterTransportPort—originally mentioned only UDP, TCP, and SCTP. RFC 9710 updates these to include DCCP (Datagram Congestion Control Protocol, defined in RFC 4340), since DCCP is also a transport protocol with 16-bit port identifiers. References to port definitions are also standardized to point consistently to the IANA service names and port numbers registry.

The forwardingStatus element had a particular problem: its registered abstract data type was unsigned8, but the description and actual usage required unsigned32. The RFC fixes the abstract data type and clarifies when reduced-size encoding is used.
sections.plainLanguage: Some descriptions were missing information about newer protocols like DCCP. Others had the wrong data type specified. These are now corrected and consistent.

sections.title: Standardizing Registry Citations
sections.content:
Many Information Elements refer to values defined in other IANA registries. For example, mplsTopLabelType uses values from the MPLS label type registry. Previously, descriptions were inconsistent: some embedded the registry URL inline, some had it in "Additional Information," and some named the registry differently than IANA did.

RFC 9710 standardizes the format. Each element now has its registry referenced in the "Additional Information" field using a consistent citation style like "See the 'MPLS label type' registry" with a URL. Registry names are aligned with current IANA names. Over 20 Information Elements receive these consistency updates, including classificationEngineId, flowEndReason, natEvent, biflowDirection, observationPointType, natType, and others.
sections.plainLanguage: When an Information Element uses values from another IANA list, the registry now always mentions that list in the same way and with the current name.

sections.title: Other Fixes
sections.content:
The RFC corrects orphaned references to removed sections. For example, collectionTimeMilliseconds originally referenced "messageScope Information Element, as defined below" but the definition was not below. This reference is removed. Similarly, messageMD5Checksum had an outdated reference that is cleaned up.

The anonymizationFlags description is updated to reference RFC 6235 instead of generic "Section 5.1." The informationElementDescription field is updated to point to the correct RFC 5610 section on string handling. Typos and formatting issues throughout the registry are also corrected—for instance, changing "ie" to "i.e." and "section Section" to just "Section."
sections.plainLanguage: References to deleted sections are removed, typos are fixed, and links point to the right RFC sections.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
IPFIX collectors need to understand new Information Elements as they are registered. The RFC notes that automated extraction of registry values (for example, using a cron job) requires that registry entries be well-formed and consistent. With these fixes, tools can reliably parse the registry to discover which Information Elements are available, what values they can take, and where to find the authoritative definitions of those values.

This also benefits human readers: a well-organized registry with consistent formatting and current links is easier to navigate and less likely to contain errors. The RFC emphasizes that these fixes enable both programmatic and manual use of the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: When the registry is clear and consistent, software can automatically read it to stay up to date with new information elements. People can also understand it faster.
